title: Dedicated reserved-pool throttling causing failed scale-ups and customer request queuing
creator: Maya Patel
description: Summary: Multiple Dedicated customers experienced prolonged request queuing and 429/503 tail errors when burst traffic exceeded reserved pool capacity. Autoscaler failed to allocate burst instances due to a race condition in reserved-pool token accounting and an aggressive burst limiter. Several SREs and customer-facing engineers were paged. This ticket tracks triage, root cause, fix, and rollout for the hotpatch and follow-ups.
incident_timeline: 2026-02-19 21:12 UTC - Pager duty alerted: increased 429 rates from dedicated endpoints in us-west-2
2026-02-19 21:20 UTC - Oncall observed queue depth spike for reserved pool 'rsv-prod-12' and connection stall metrics rising
2026-02-19 21:30 UTC - Manual mitigation: temporarily increased burst limit for affected pool, transient relief observed
2026-02-20 02:05 UTC - Customer escalation from Acme Analytics and NeoBank complaining persistent throttles during a scheduled traffic surge

2026-02-20 08:45 UTC - Engineering reproduced locally: simultaneous burst grants from two control-plane replicas caused over-decrement of pool tokens; autoscaler aborted new allocation on subsequent token validation failures
2026-02-24 16:00 UTC - Hotfix PR opened (see pr_links), unit and integration tests added to reproduce race; patch landed in canary runtime-1.19-canary-3
2026-02-25 09:30 UTC - Canary run showed stable token accounting and no queuing under synthetic load; rollout to us-west-2 staged
2026-02-26 14:00 UTC - Full rollout to all Dedicated regions completed; monitoring for regressions ongoing
reproduction_steps: Deploy a reserved pool with burst_limit=150 and baseline_capacity=50
Start 3 parallel clients each requesting large concurrent batches to exceed 200 simultaneous active streams
Observe token accounting in control-plane: two replicas grant burst tokens concurrently leading to negative token count briefly
See autoscaler abort new instance creation due to token validation check failing with stale token state
root_cause_summary: A race condition between control-plane replicas when handling burst grants could transiently drive the reserved-pool token counter negative. The autoscaler validated token state using a read-modify-write path that assumed monotonic counters and aborted allocation if validation failed. An additional protective burst limiter introduced last quarter (to prevent runaway burst costs) had overly aggressive backoff and prevented retrying allocations, so failed allocations piled up as queued requests.
mitigations_applied: Temporary increase of burst limit for impacted pools to reduce immediate queuing
Disabled aggressive burst backoff in control-plane config for affected clusters
Added emergency runbook steps for SREs to perform controlled pool expansion when token anomalies detected
pr_links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4182 - fix(reserved-pool): atomic token updates and idempotent grants
https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4185 - test(dedicated): add concurrency regression test for burst grants
https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1294 - ops: rollback temporary burst-backoff change and add canary gating
deploy_plan: Canary -> us-west-2 -> us-east-1 -> eu-west-1. Canary validated with synthetic load and two-hour observation window. Rollout steps include: 1) deploy runtime-1.19-canary-3 to canary machines, 2) run automated concurrency test suite, 3) promote to region when metrics stable for 2h, 4) monitor queue depth and token counters closely; rollback if 2x baseline 95th latency or SLO breach.
monitoring_and_alerting_changes: Add dedicated metric reserved_pool.token_invariant_violations with alert when >0
Instrument autoscaler allocation failures with reason labels (token_validation, quota, capacity) and create a PagerDuty mapping for token_validation
Dashboards updated: reserved pool heatmap and pending_allocations histogram
customer_notifications: 2026-02-20 10:15 UTC - Status update sent to affected customers (Acme Analytics, NeoBank, SkyShop) with temporary workaround and engineering timeline
2026-02-26 18:00 UTC - Postmortem and resolution email with mitigation steps and SLA credit offer sent to customers
Customer success follow-ups scheduled: 3-week check-in and traffic replay review
resolution_summary: Patch implemented to make token grants atomic across control-plane replicas and to remove the aggressive one-shot burst backoff. Integration tests added to prevent regression. Rollout completed to all Dedicated regions; queued requests dropped to baseline and 95th latency returned to SLO. SLA credits offered to impacted customers and CS is coordinating remediation for any lost requests.
